中年男性自杀率创历史新高

Suicide rates highest ever among middle-aged men

AI 作者 ivewonyoung 热度 540 回复 763 2026/10/15 03:03
打开原帖 打开外部链接 JSON

摘要

  • Suicide rates among middle-aged men are higher than ever, new figures have revealed.Men in their early 50s were more likely to die by suicide than anyone else last year, according to data from the Office for National Statistics.There were also increases in suicides among pensioners, with the biggest rise among those aged 75 and older, while the rates among men under 45 fell slightly.Mark Winstanley, the chief executive of Rethink Mental Illness, said the rate of deaths by suicide remained “stubbornly high”.He said: “Every suicide is a devastating tragedy, and these figures are a stark reminder that many people are reaching crisis point without getting the help they need.”The reasons behind suicide were “complex”, he said, but added that many people were “facing significant pressures in their lives, including financial issues, job insecurity, rising housing costs, loneliness and poor mental health”.Suicide rate highest on recordMr Winstanley added: “While these factors affect everyone differently, they can contribute to distress and overwhelm, and leave people at risk of suicide.”The data, which cover England and Wales, showed that 6,162 suicide deaths had been registered in 2025. This was down from 6,190 last year, but the overall rate remained broadly the same at 11.3 deaths per 100,000 people.The stats watchdog uses deaths per 100,000 people to calculate changing rates while accounting for changes in the size of the population.Almost a third of the deaths were among men aged 45 to 64, which was up by 49 compared with 2024. The rate increased to 23.8 per 100,000, up from 23.2 the year before and the highest on record since data collection began in 1981.For men aged 50 to 54 specifically, the rate increased to 28, suggesting this group was at the highest risk.
  • Men continued to be more than three times as likely to take their own lives as women overall. Among middle-aged women, there were 553 deaths – a rate of seven per 100,000, which was the same as 2024.Sonya Trivedy, the executive director of external engagement at Samaritans, said the figures “show that suicide rates are among the highest recorded rates this century”.She said: “The evidence is clear that successive governments have failed to deliver on their promise to reduce suicide rates and make suicide prevention a priority. Today must act as a wake up call. The current approach is not working; we need meaningful action and proper funding if lives are to be saved.”The data show a growing gap in suicide rates between middle-aged men and those aged 25 to 44.

munificent 2026/10/15 04:22
因为它非常相关，所以我将解释一下我上周发表的评论：

我认为问题的很大一部分在于，在社会眼中，中年男性正处于他们对成功的期望的顶峰，而我们正在经历一个很难定义成功的时期，更不用说实现了。

社会学中有一个名字：失范[1]。埃米尔·涂尔干 (Émile Durkheim) 在工业革命后不久写的《自杀》一书中创造了这个词。

在巨大变革的时代，我们视为理所当然的生活组织原则的一套规范和规则被连根拔起。就好像我们一生玩过的棋盘游戏的所有棋子、令牌和规则都被扫出了桌子，为新游戏腾出空间，但新游戏还没有建立起来。在此期间，我们都感到不安。轮到我们走棋了，但我们不知道游戏规则，也不知道该走什么棋。我们感受到要玩好游戏的巨大压力，但不知道如何去做。

过去，这些转变已经结束，社会总体上恢复了某种稳定感。一个新的棋盘游戏被设置，新的棋子被分发，我们学习玩新游戏。我希望人工智能很快就能达到这一点，但革命似乎会越来越快。

我认为，对于很多人来说，感觉就像是在我们辛辛苦苦玩了社会告诉我们的游戏之后，应该能够在功劳簿上休息一下的时候，规则已经被从我们身上撕下来，任何前进的安全感都消失了。我们觉得自己太老了，无法及时学习新的游戏规则来玩好游戏，但还没有老到能够戒掉游戏。

这是一个心理上非常困难的时期。

[1]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anomie

Because it's highly relevant, I'm going to paraphrase a comment I made last week:

I think a big part of the problem is that middle-aged men are at the apex of their expectations to be successful in the eyes of society, and we are living through a period of time where success is very hard to define, much less attain.

There is a name for this in sociology: anomie [1]. Émile Durkheim coined it in his book Suicide, written not too long after the Industrial Revolution.

In times of great change, the set of norms and rules that we take for granted as an organizing principle of our lives get uprooted. It's as if all of the pieces and tokens and rules of the board game we played our whole lives are swept off the table to make room for a new game, but the new game has not been set up yet. In that interim, we all feel a sense of unease. It is our turn to move, but we don't know the rules of the game or what moves to make. We feel intense pressure to play the game well, but don't know how.

In the past, these transitions have ended and society has generally returned to some sense of stability. A new board game gets set up, new pieces doled out, we learn to play the new game. I hope we get to that point with AI soon, but the revolutions seem to keep coming faster and faster.

I think for a lot of men, it feels like just at the time when we should be able to rest on our laurels a bit after having worked so hard to play the game society told us to, the rules have been ripped out from under us and any sense of security going forward is lost. We feel too old to learn the new rules of the game in time to play well, but not old enough to be able to abstain from playing.

It's a psychologically very difficult time.

[1]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anomie
